title: Judge leniency as IV for incarceration on recidivism

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
**Instrumental Variables (IV)** using judge leniency as an instrument for incarceration. The key assumptions are: (1) **Relevance**: lenient judges are less likely to incarcerate defendants, (2) **Exclusion restriction**: judge assignment only affects recidivism through the incarceration decision (not directly), and (3) **Monotonicity**: judge leniency affects incarceration in the same direction for all defendants. This leverages the quasi-random assignment of cases to judges with different sentencing tendencies.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(AER)
library(stargazer)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s23_data.csv")

# Check data structure
print("Data summary:")
print(summary(data))
print(paste("Sample size:", nrow(data)))

# First stage: Judge leniency predicting incarceration
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = data)
print("\n=== FIRST STAGE RESULTS ===")
print(summary(first_stage))

# Check first stage F-statistic
f_stat <- summary(first_stage)$fstatistic[1]
print(paste("First stage F-statistic:", round(f_stat, 2)))

# Reduced form: Judge leniency predicting recidivism
reduced_form <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = data)
print("\n=== REDUCED FORM RESULTS ===")
print(summary(reduced_form))

# Two-stage least squares (2SLS) estimation
iv_model <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = data)
print("\n=== IV (2SLS) RESULTS ===")
print(summary(iv_model))

# Extract key coefficient
iv_coeff <- coef(iv_model)["x"]
iv_se <- summary(iv_model)$coefficients["x", "Std. Error"]
iv_pvalue <- summary(iv_model)$coefficients["x", "Pr(>|t|)"]

print("\n=== MAIN RESULT ===")
print(paste("IV Coefficient (Incarceration → Recidivism):", round(iv_coeff, 4)))
print(paste("Standard Error:", round(iv_se, 4)))
print(paste("P-value:", round(iv_pvalue, 4)))

# Compare with OLS (biased estimate)
ols_model <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = data)
ols_coeff <- coef(ols_model)["x"]
print(paste("OLS Coefficient (for comparison):", round(ols_coeff, 4)))

# Robustness checks
print("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===")

# 1. Test instrument strength (rule of thumb: F > 10)
print(paste("Instrument strength test - F-stat:", round(f_stat, 2), 
            ifelse(f_stat > 10, "(STRONG)", "(WEAK)")))

# 2. IV without controls
iv_no_controls <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = data)
iv_coeff_no_controls <- coef(iv_no_controls)["x"]
print(paste("IV coefficient without controls:", round(iv_coeff_no_controls, 4)))

# 3. Check for balance in judge assignment (reduced form should be significant if IV works)
rf_coeff <- coef(reduced_form)["z"]
rf_pvalue <- summary(reduced_form)$coefficients["z", "Pr(>|t|)"]
print(paste("Reduced form coefficient:", round(rf_coeff, 4), 
            "p-value:", round(rf_pvalue, 4)))

# Summary table
print("\n=== SUMMARY TABLE ===")
results_table <- data.frame(
  Model = c("OLS", "First Stage", "Reduced Form", "IV (2SLS)"),
  Coefficient = c(round(ols_coeff, 4), 
                 round(coef(first_stage)["z"], 4),
                 round(rf_coeff, 4), 
                 round(iv_coeff, 4)),
  Std_Error = c(round(summary(ols_model)$coefficients["x", "Std. Error"], 4),
               round(summary(first_stage)$coefficients["z", "Std. Error"], 4),
               round(summary(reduced_form)$coefficients["z", "Std. Error"], 4),
               round(iv_se, 4))
)
print(results_table)
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a **positive coefficient** (around 0.3-0.7) indicating that incarceration **increases** recidivism. This aligns with criminological theory suggesting incarceration may have criminogenic effects through social stigma, human capital deterioration, and exposure to criminal networks. The IV estimate should be larger in magnitude than OLS if there's negative selection bias (worse offenders more likely to be incarcerated). The first stage should show a strong negative relationship between judge leniency and incarceration probability (F-stat > 10 for instrument relevance).

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: IV/2SLS — judge leniency instrument; LATE for marginal defendants; test exclusion restriction carefully
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Incarceration increases recidivism for marginal defendants (criminogenic effect)
_ground_truth.main_effect: Incarceration raises 3-year recidivism probability by ~15pp for compliers
